checks.label: the delivery is not complete
the delivery driver is ready to drive

limits: The action begins exactly one ten-mile interval; autonomous processes determine whether it advances or stalls.
The action does not itself inspect or consume fuel.
The model assumes the represented driver remains linked to the vehicle named by components.driver.vehicle_ref.
Route movement is limited to the represented ten-mile interval and does not model speed, traffic, or detours.
mechanics.rationale: A drive attempt begins one represented ten-mile driving interval. Fuel feasibility is resolved by autonomous processes after the interval begins.
semantic_bindings: One drive action requests one ten-mile interval.
Driving status records the begun interval.
Fuel consumption is 10 miles multiplied by the represented 0.04 gallons per mile.
Movement of the driver and linked vehicle occurs together in one process.
tests: A ready delivery driver with an incomplete delivery enters driving status.
A driver whose delivery is complete is refused.
A driver who is already driving, refueling, or otherwise not ready is refused.
Low fuel does not refuse the action; the subsequent driving process stalls the interval if less than 0.4 gallons is represented.

checks.label: the delivery is not complete
the delivery driver is not already refueling
the delivery driver and gas station are on the same route
the delivery driver is at the gas station
the gas station offers fuel
the requested amount is one gallon

limits: Only a one-gallon request is supported because no represented field stores an arbitrary pending refuel amount.
Beginning the attempt does not guarantee sufficient station stock or tank space.
The selected station must be a represented gas station at the driver's route position.
Payment, price, and refueling duration are not represented.
mechanics.rationale: A refuel attempt may begin only at the represented gas station and is limited to one gallon so the requested quantity can be represented without inventing storage for a pending amount. Stock and tank feasibility are resolved autonomously.
semantic_bindings: The station field identifies the represented gas station participant.
The amount field is constrained to one gallon.
Refueling status records the begun attempt.
Successful completion transfers one gallon from station stock to the linked vehicle.
tests: At route position 60, a non-refueling driver can begin a one-gallon refuel attempt at the gas station.
A driver away from the station is refused.
An amount other than one gallon is refused.
Zero station stock does not refuse the attempt; the autonomous failure process resolves it.
A nearly full tank does not refuse the attempt; the autonomous capacity failure process resolves it.

the delivery vehicle is operational
the delivery vehicle has enough fuel for this interval
the delivery driver has not reached the route end
the delivery vehicle uses the represented fuel rate

processes.rationale: Each started driving interval advances the driver and linked vehicle ten miles, consumes 0.4 gallons at the represented rate, updates the fuel fraction for the represented 15-gallon tank, and counts one driving tick when enough fuel exists.

checks.label: the delivery driver has begun driving
the delivery vehicle lacks fuel for this interval
the delivery driver has not reached the route end

processes.rationale: A begun driving interval stalls without movement when the linked vehicle lacks the 0.4 gallons required for ten miles.

processes.rationale: A pending one-gallon refuel transfers fuel from the co-located gas station to the linked vehicle when stock and tank space suffice.

checks.label: the delivery driver is refueling

processes.rationale: A pending refuel attempt fails without transferring fuel when the represented station has less than one gallon.

processes.rationale: A pending one-gallon refuel fails without transferring fuel when adding a gallon would exceed the represented 15-gallon tank.
